hook.line: At the clinic, everyone seems to be telling Hernando what he may and may not do. Doctors, nurses and signs on the wall all use the same short frame: a verb of advice or permission, then a plain infinitive.

examples.en: They didn't let you in. (to a friend)
The doctor banned me from smoking.
I advise you to wait a little. (to a friend)

examples.es: La doctora nos recomienda comer menos sal.
examples.en: The doctor recommends that we eat less salt.
They don't let you all smoke here.

rule:
To tell someone what to do, or what they may do, use a verb of advice or permission, a little word for the person, and an infinitive.

*recomendar*, *aconsejar*: advise. *Le recomiendo descansar*.
*permitir*: allow. *No me permitieron entrar* ("they didn't let me in").
*prohibir*: ban. *El médico me prohibió fumar*.

The little word (*me*, *te*, *le*, *nos*, *les*) says who is allowed, advised or banned. That same person is the one who does the infinitive: *Le recomiendo descansar* means you rest.

English needs "that you" or "to": "I recommend that you rest". Spanish just uses the infinitive.
smallPrint: Teachers call the little word the indirect object, and the infinitive a complement of verbs of influence.

I recommend that I rest.
I recommend that he rests.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right word and type the whole sentence: *Le ___ descansar.* (*recomiendo* or *prohibió*) I recommend that you rest. (formal)
Choose the right word and type the whole sentence: *El médico me ___ fumar.* (*prohibió* or *aconsejó*) The doctor banned me from smoking.
Type in Spanish: They didn't let you in. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Te* is your friend, and *entrar* stays as an infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I advise you to wait a little. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Te* is your friend, and *esperar* is the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about us: *El médico me prohibió fumar.*
yourTurn.why: Only the little word changes: *nos* for "us".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it polite, for someone you call *usted*: *Te recomiendo descansar.*
Make it negative: *Les permiten fumar aquí.*

pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish puts the infinitive right after the verb, with no *a* in between.
The person goes in the little word before the verb: *le*.
Without a little word like *te* we don't know who was refused; add it.

personal: Tell us one thing someone *te recomienda* or *te prohíbe* doing, with the little word *te* or *me*.
